Pile Cap Design

OCR load → pile quantity → typical pile arrangement → preliminary pile-cap thickness & bottom reinforcement

Engineering scope: pile quantity is based on the entered allowable single-pile axial capacity and concentric axial OCR load. Cap thickness/reinforcement uses simplified ACI-style sectional shear/flexure checks for preliminary sizing. Group efficiency, settlement, downdrag, uplift/lateral load, seismic effects, pile/column dowels and detailed strut-and-tie design are not included. Two- and three-pile caps, and very deep caps, should be verified by a project structural engineer using a strut-and-tie model.
OCR footing loads in this suite are normally treated as kips. Change the load unit below only if your source numbers are in metric ton-force (tonf).
Metric ton-force: 1 ton = 2.20462 kip.
Excel convention: Ec = 4700√f'c (MPa), K = EA/L.

Pile Cap Structural Inputs

Circular: s = factor × D. Rectangular precast: sx = factor × Bx, sy = factor × By. Staggered rows auto-calculate the vertical row pitch so the actual diagonal C/C is maintained (for equal spacing: Y = 0.866S).
Center → edge is calculated automatically as ½ pile size + this face overhang.
BNBC 2020 + international geometry basis: BNBC 2020 commentary Sec. 3.10.1.19 recommends minimum pile spacing of 2.5B c/c; this tool defaults to 3.0B c/c, consistent with common FHWA practice to reduce pile-group/installation interaction. BNBC Sec. 3.10.1.20 requires the cap to extend at least 100 mm beyond the pile face and pile heads to be embedded at least 75 mm into the cap; IBC 2024 similarly uses 4 in (102 mm) cap overhang and 3 in (76 mm) embedment. Exact pile-count layouts are not prescribed as fixed code diagrams; Auto layout below uses symmetric, centroid-balanced typical arrangements. Example: 10 piles = 3–4–3 staggered, not 5×2.

Soil

Multi-borehole SPT bearing capacity + Bangladesh-context sand pile screening

Engineering notice: This is a preliminary screening tool. Final foundation selection and allowable pressure must be checked for settlement, structural loads, footing dimensions, groundwater, liquefaction/seismic issues and project-specific geotechnical testing. Values shown as “thumb rule” are not BNBC-prescribed fixed design values.

1) Project + Global Settings

Actual footing base level. Surcharge is calculated at this depth — not at the SPT sample depth.

2) Borehole / SPT Input

Add as many boreholes as needed. At the proposed footing base, each borehole is checked using conservative bracketing SPT data. Soil below the base is then checked through the selected pressure-influence zone using a simplified 2:1 stress-spread screen. The lowest borehole pressure limit governs the one Site TSF. A deeper good layer does not automatically increase shallow-footing capacity; the footing must reach it or the weak layer must be engineered.

বাংলা নোট: কোন ইনপুট কোথা থেকে নেবেন

Moist unit weight γ (pcf): সবচেয়ে ভালো হলো bore log/lab report-এর moist বা bulk unit weight নেওয়া। রিপোর্টে না থাকলে শুধু preliminary screening-এর জন্য সাধারণ alluvial sand/silty soil-এ প্রায় 110–120 pcf ধরে শুরু করা যায়; এই টুলে default 115 pcf। Final design-এ measured value ব্যবহার করবেন।
Saturated unit weight γsat (pcf): groundwater-এর নিচের soil-এর জন্য lab/report value ব্যবহার করুন। না থাকলে preliminary হিসেবে প্রায় 118–128 pcf range দেখা যায়; টুলে default 120 pcf।
SPT hammer energy ratio ER (%): drillers/SPT report-এ hammer energy calibration থাকলে সেটাই দিন। N60 হচ্ছে 60% reference energy-তে normalized N। Energy জানা না থাকলে ER=60% ব্যবহার করলে input N-কে N60 ধরে নেওয়ার মতো আচরণ করবে—কিন্তু এটি measured correction নয়।
Clay Su factor (kPa per N60): SPT-N থেকে Su বের করা খুব approximate। Vane shear, UU/UC test বা lab Su থাকলে অবশ্যই সেটি ব্যবহার করবেন। শুধু screening-এর জন্য প্রায় 5–7 kPa per N60 range ব্যবহার করা হয়; এখানে default 6.25 রাখা হয়েছে। Soft/sensitive clay-এ এই correlation ভুল হতে পারে।
Factor of Safety: এই tool-এ FS=3.0 default রাখা হয়েছে preliminary shallow bearing screening-এর জন্য। এটি সব project-এর জন্য BNBC fixed value হিসেবে ধরা যাবে না; design method, failure mode ও settlement অনুযায়ী engineer ঠিক করবেন।

Multiple Borehole + Soil Pressure Transfer → একটি TSF

১) Proposed footing base depth-এই surcharge ধরা হয়; SPT sample যদি আরও নিচে থাকে, সেই sample depth-কে foundation depth বানানো হয় না। ২) Base level-এর উপরে/নিচে nearest bracketing SPT data থেকে conservative strength নেওয়া হয়। ৩) Footing base-এর নিচে default 2B influence zone পর্যন্ত SPT rows দেখা হয়। ৪) Simplified 2:1 stress spread দিয়ে নিচের layer-এ footing pressure-এর কত অংশ পৌঁছায় তার factor I ধরা হয়। ৫) প্রতিটি borehole-এর pressure limit বের করে সবচেয়ে কম borehole value Site TSF হয়।

গুরুত্বপূর্ণ: নিচে ভালো soil থাকলেই উপরের দুর্বল layer-এ বসানো shallow footing-এর TSF বাড়ানো হয় না। দুর্বল layer যদি footing base-এই থাকে, সেটাই base bearing control করতে পারে। আবার নিচে খুব দুর্বল/compressible layer থাকলে stress bulb-এর মধ্যে সেটি settlement/pressure-transfer risk তৈরি করতে পারে। এই tool layered-soil finite-element analysis নয়; conservative screening.

Foundation depth / pile recommendation logic

Site TSF ≥ 1.0: default screen-এ sand pile recommend করা হবে না। Proposed depth-এ shallow footing/raft candidate দেখাবে, তবে structural service pressure ও settlement check লাগবে.

Site TSF < 1.0: tool current depth থেকে max practical shallow depth পর্যন্ত profile scan করবে। যদি সব borehole consider করে ≥1.0 TSF-এর একটি shallower practical solution পাওয়া যায়, আগে deeper shallow footing recommend করবে। যদি ভালো shallow layer না পাওয়া যায়, soil type, weak-zone depth ও storey count দেখে sand pile / engineered ground improvement / deep pile comparison suggest করবে।

Storey count actual column load নয়। Final footing-vs-pile decision-এর জন্য column reactions, footing size, settlement, groundwater, liquefaction, negative skin friction এবং constructability লাগবে।

BNBC-aligned Thumb Rule Guide — কীভাবে ব্যবহার করবেন

গুরুত্বপূর্ণ: নিচের diameter/spacing/FM সংখ্যা BNBC-এর mandatory table নয়। এগুলো Bangladesh project/case-study practice থেকে নেওয়া preliminary trial ranges। BNBC-compliant final design-এর জন্য site investigation, settlement, seismic/liquefaction, groundwater, load এবং verification test দরকার।

SPT অনুযায়ী quick soil reading

Sand / silty sand: N60 ≤ 4 very loose, 5–10 loose, 11–30 medium dense, 31–50 dense, >50 very dense — qualitative screening.

Clay / silty clay: N60 < 2 very soft, 2–4 soft, 5–8 medium, 9–15 stiff, 16–30 very stiff, >30 hard — SPT-only consistency estimate is uncertain.

Sand pile কোথায় বেশি যুক্তিযুক্ত

Loose sand/silty sand (বিশেষ করে N60 ≤ 10) এবং low-rise building হলে sand compaction/displacement pile একটি reasonable candidate হতে পারে। Soft clay-এ sand pile কাজ করতে পারে, কিন্তু সেখানে simple N-value দিয়ে “safe” বলা যায় না; composite-ground/settlement analysis এবং field trial দরকার। Organic soil/peat, uncontrolled fill, খুব thick soft layer, high seismic/liquefaction concern বা 7+ storey building হলে এই screening tool দিয়ে sand pile finalise করবেন না।

Bangladesh-context preliminary trial range

1–3 storey + loose granular soil: trial starting range প্রায় 10–12 inch diameter, 24–30 inch c/c spacing, clean non-plastic sand; FM ~2.0–2.6 preferred as a practical starting band. Improvement depth should pass through the weak/loose layer; termination depth must come from bore log, not from storey count alone.

4–6 storey: sand pile may still be technically possible in some profiles, but this tool will mark it Conditional. Diameter/spacing should be engineered after load, settlement and area-replacement checks; post-improvement SPT/plate-load verification is strongly recommended.

7 storey or more: SPT + soil type + storey count alone is not enough to approve sand pile. Compare engineered ground improvement with RCC pile/deep foundation and verify settlement and seismic performance.

Sand quality note

Bangladesh granular-pile studies have reported better performance with coarser Sylhet-type sand (one field study reported FM about 2.58) compared with much finer local sand. Therefore this tool recommends clean, non-plastic, relatively coarse sand and flags low-FM/fine material as less desirable. Project specification should use sieve analysis, fines content and compaction criteria—not FM alone.

References / basis for screening logic

• Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC 2020): use as governing code framework for geotechnical investigation/foundation design. This tool does not claim a BNBC fixed sand-pile diameter/spacing/FM table.

• Md. Ikramul Hoque & Muhammed Alamgir, field performance of granular pile in Bangladesh: rammed-compaction granular piles; reported Sylhet sand FM ≈ 2.58 and local finer sand FM ≈ 1.13.

• Bangladesh case study (2023): locally constructed sand compaction piles around 250 mm diameter at about 600 mm spacing were used for a project-specific soft-ground solution.

• Bangladesh southwest study/preprint (2026): 300 mm diameter, 8.25 m long sand compaction piles were field-tested; project-specific geometry and verification were central to the study.

• Dhaka MRT soil-improvement case study (2026): project-specific ground improvement used much larger displacement/SCP elements; reinforces that geometry is site/method dependent.

Preliminary screening only. Do not issue construction drawings or foundation approval from this module alone.

Beam

Straight Bars (full length)
Extra Bars (at supports)
Extra Top/Bottom lengths follow standard BNBC/ACI curtailment guidance (Exterior support L/4, Interior support L/3, Extra Bottom 70–75% of clear span). This does not add the extra development length (Ld) / hook length into the column at exterior supports — add that manually to the length field if needed.

Slab

Main Bar (cranked / alternate bar system)
Runs across the Width, spaced along the Length. Of the total bars, alternate bars are cranked (bent up near supports) to serve as the negative-moment (top) steel — so no separate "extra top" bars are needed in this direction. The other half stay straight along the bottom.
Distribution Bar (top steel only, at supports)
Runs across the Length, spaced along the Width — placed only near the supports as negative-moment steel (no bottom mesh role here, since the cranked Main bars already cover the bottom). Length is curtailed to a fraction of its own span (Length).

Concrete quantities use the standard dry-volume method (wet volume × 1.54), 1 bag cement = 1.25 cft. Rod weight uses the standard formula D²/162 kg per meter. This covers main/longitudinal reinforcement only — stirrups/ties are not included. Please verify results before use.

আপনার শেখা 14.5 ft × 7.5 ft × 6 ft reservoir example অনুযায়ী vertical wall bending, horizontal wall action এবং bottom slab design একই জায়গায়।

একই depth-এ water pressure পুরো long wall-এ থাকে। Course-note expression-এ long wall-এর দুই half (7.25 ft + 7.25 ft) middle section-এর action হিসেবে একসাথে দেখানো হয়েছে।

Important distinction

Pressure intensity মাঝখানে বেশি নয়. একই depth-এ p = γh একই। এখানে 7.25 + 7.25 হলো দুই half-length-এর structural action representation। নিচের calculator আপনার দেওয়া class-note workflow reproduce করে; final water-retaining structure design project-specific code checks দিয়ে verify করতে হবে।

Bottom pressure: p = γh
Vertical wall moment: M = γh³/6
Horizontal note expression: F = γh(L/2 + L/2)

Appendix SSec. 5.9.1.2Auto Save
Code scope: এটি capacity ও practical internal dimension-এর preliminary calculator। RCC wall/slab design, uplift, soil pressure, waterproofing, pipe sizing, fire-system approval এবং authority clearance licensed professionals দ্বারা project-specificভাবে করতে হবে।
SANITATION • APPENDIX S

Septic Tank — BNBC Equation 8.S.1

V = PQt + Psv. Minimum capacity, geometry, clear space এবং chamber recommendation automatically applied.

BNBC checks: minimum liquid capacity 2000 L; width ≥ 1 m; liquid depth ≥ 1 m; length ≥ 3W and recommended ≤ 4W; 300 mm clear space above liquid; two chambers recommended above 3000 L; residential users ≤ 300.
WATER STORAGE • SEC. 5.9.1.2

Underground Water Reservoir (UGR)

BNBC domestic water demand, selected storage days এবং entered fire reserve থেকে UGR capacity ও practical internal dimension হিসাব করুন।

BNBC basis: UGR = selected daily demand + entered 1-hour firefighting reserve for tall buildings. Normal code basis is 1 day; 2–3 days may be selected for emergency storage. Storage tanks should have at least two compartments/units for alternative cleaning. Roof tank reference = ½ daily demand + fire reserve.

Axial Strength ΦPn (kip)

Theme-matched strength comparison with clearer scale and value formatting.

Axial capacity uses the short tied‑column formula common to BNBC 2020 / ACI 318: ΦPn = 0.80 × 0.65 × [0.85f'c(Ag−Ast) + fy·Ast]. This is pure axial capacity (no bending/slenderness/eccentricity considered) — use it for relative comparison, not final design. Reinforcement ratio (Ast/Ag) should stay within BNBC's 1%–8% range; a warning appears below if a column falls outside it.
